summary: Small US recruiting agencies run high call volume with few operations staff. The market splits into recruiting platforms with bundled notes, general transcription services, and applicant tracking system add-ons. The open gap is a recruiting-specific assistant that extracts candidate requirements and writes structured follow-up actions into the ATS.

competitors.name: Recruiting platforms with built-in notes
competitors.positioning: Bundle scheduling, candidate messaging, and notes

competitors.name: General transcription services
competitors.positioning: Broad language support with little recruiting logic

market_opportunities: Small agencies lack structured intake notes and retype them into the ATS
Structured notes reduce rework and improve candidate handoffs
A paid pilot can prove time savings within one hiring cycle
trends: Remote intake calls are common, so recordings are already available
Buyers expect data controls for candidate personal data
Integration quality is a primary purchase criterion
Agencies prefer tools that work with their current ATS

claims.text: Human-resources specialists are a documented US occupation with published employment outlook data.

evidence_refs.title: Occupational Outlook Handbook: Human Resources Specialists

claims.text: Small US recruiting agencies are business establishments covered by Census Bureau small-business statistics.
Handling candidate personal data requires a breach response plan consistent with federal guidance.

evidence_refs.title: Federal Trade Commission: Data Breach Response

claims.text: Talent acquisition is a documented recruiting function with established practice guidance.
The open gap is a recruiting-specific assistant that extracts candidate requirements and sends structured follow-up actions into the ATS.
A narrow tool for small agencies can win on fit and speed, not on feature breadth.
The launch should lead with ATS integration and data handling, not with model quality alone.

assumptions: Small agencies will accept a paid pilot within 90 days
Remote recordings of intake calls are already available in pilot agencies
limitations: No primary market-size estimate is provided
No survey of agency owners was run for this reference trial
